what_its_for: This device turns liquid medicine into a fine mist so you can breathe it directly into your lungs. It is commonly used to treat breathing problems such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), bronchitis, and other lung conditions. Breathing medicine in as a mist helps it work faster and more directly in your airways compared to swallowing a pill.
how_to_take: 1. Wash your hands well with soap and water before handling the nebulizer. 2. Place your liquid medicine into the small medicine cup (also called the nebulizer cup or reservoir) as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. 3. Attach the mouthpiece or face mask securely to the cup. 4. Sit up straight in a comfortable chair. 5. Place the mouthpiece in your mouth and seal your lips around it, OR place the face mask snugly over your nose and mouth. 6. Squeeze the rubber bulb slowly and steadily to release the mist, then breathe in slowly and deeply through your mouth. 7. Hold your breath for 2 to 3 seconds before breathing out slowly. 8. Repeat until all the medicine in the cup is gone (treatment usually takes 10 to 15 minutes). 9. After each use, take apart the device and clean all parts thoroughly with warm soapy water, rinse well, and allow to air dry completely on a clean towel.
dosing: The amount of medicine and how often you use the nebulizer depends on the specific medicine your doctor prescribed. Always follow the exact instructions given by your doctor or pharmacist. Do not add more medicine than directed, and do not use the nebulizer more often than prescribed. If you are unsure how much medicine to use, ask your pharmacist before your first treatment.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled treatment, use the nebulizer as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled treatment, skip the missed one and go back to your regular schedule. Never double up doses to make up for a missed treatment. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store the nebulizer device in a clean, dry place away from dust and moisture. Keep it out of direct sunlight and away from extreme heat. Store your liquid medicine as directed on its label — some medicines need to be kept in the refrigerator, while others can be kept at room temperature. Keep medicine and the device out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date on your medicine and do not use it if it has expired.
what_to_avoid: Do not use tap water to mix your medicine unless specifically told to do so — use sterile saline or distilled water as directed. Do not share your nebulizer device with anyone else, as this can spread germs and infection. Avoid smoking or being around smoke while using the nebulizer, as it can make your breathing worse. Do not use the nebulizer near open flames or flammable materials. Avoid skipping cleaning steps, as a dirty nebulizer can grow bacteria and mold that could make you very sick. Do not use a cracked, broken, or damaged device.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if: your breathing does not improve or gets worse after a treatment; you feel your heart beating faster than normal or you feel shaky, dizzy, or lightheaded after a treatment; you develop chest pain, tightness, or pressure; you feel short of breath even after using the nebulizer; you notice your lips or fingernails turning blue or gray; you need to use the nebulizer much more often than prescribed; or you have any new or worsening symptoms that concern you. If you have a severe breathing emergency, call 911 immediately.
when_it_works: The mist from the nebulizer begins to work as soon as you breathe it in. Most people begin to feel relief from breathing difficulty within a few minutes of starting a treatment. The full benefit of the medicine depends on the specific drug being used — some medicines provide quick, short-term relief, while others work slowly over time to control symptoms and prevent flare-ups. Talk to your doctor if you feel the treatments are not helping as expected.
special_populations: Children: Children should always be supervised by an adult during nebulizer treatments. A face mask may be easier for young children who cannot hold a mouthpiece in their mouth. Make sure the mask fits properly to ensure the child gets the full dose of medicine. Elderly patients: Older adults should sit upright during treatments to help the medicine reach deep into the lungs. If you have arthritis or difficulty with hand strength, ask your pharmacist about easier ways to handle the device. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Always tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before starting any new medicine in the nebulizer. Patients with heart conditions: Some nebulized medicines can affect heart rate, so let your doctor know about any heart problems before starting treatment.
